events.title: Alfonso I of Aragon takes Zaragoza from the Almoravids
events.description: King Alfonso I of Aragon, known as the Battler, conquered Zaragoza, the most important Almoravid city in north-eastern Spain, and made it the capital of his kingdom. Its fall marked the deterioration of the Almoravids' northern front.

events.title: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty
events.description: Kublai Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan and Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan for his realm in China. The Yuan completed the conquest of the Southern Song in 1279 and ruled China until 1368.

events.title: An uprising against forced conversions breaks out in Granada
events.description: In Granada's Albaicín, a crowd killed a constable taking a woman away for questioning after she cried out that she was being forced to become Christian. It began the Rebellion of the Alpujarras against mass forced conversions.

events.title: Cromwell's Whitehall Conference on readmitting Jews ends
events.description: A conference of English merchants, clergymen and lawyers called by Oliver Cromwell ended its debate on readmitting Jews to England, finding no law that prevented their return. Edward I's Edict of Expulsion had banned them in 1290.

events.title: Americans observe the first national day of thanksgiving
events.description: The Continental Congress set aside 18 December as a day of thanksgiving for the victory at Saratoga. It was the first such national observance by the new United States.
events.html: The Continental Congress set aside 18 December as a day of thanksgiving for the victory at Saratoga. It was the first such national observance by the new United States.

events.title: The 13th Amendment abolishing slavery is proclaimed
events.description: Secretary of State William Seward certified that the 13th Amendment had been ratified by the required number of states. It abolished slavery throughout the United States, freeing about four million people.
events.html: Secretary of State William Seward certified that the 13th Amendment had been ratified by the required number of states. It abolished slavery throughout the United States, freeing about four million people.

events.title: An earthquake and tsunami strike Keelung and Taipei in Taiwan
events.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake off northern Taiwan seriously damaged Keelung and Taipei, and its tsunami drowned hundreds; the death toll was estimated at 580. It is possibly the only confirmed widely destructive and deadly tsunami in Taiwan's history.

events.title: 'Piltdown Man' is presented to the Geological Society
events.description: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward announced fossils from Piltdown in Sussex as an early human ancestor. In 1953 they were exposed as a forgery combining a human skull and an orang-utan jaw.

events.title: The Battle of Verdun ends
events.description: After ten months of fighting, French counter-attacks closed the Battle of Verdun. About 700,000 French and German soldiers were killed, wounded or missing, and the front was almost back where it began.

events.title: The US launches SCORE, the first communications satellite
events.description: An Atlas rocket placed Project SCORE in orbit. The next day it broadcast a recorded Christmas message from President Eisenhower, the first voice transmitted from space.

song: Romanians; the revolutionaries of 1848; the Romanian state
The national anthem of Romania: a poem of the 1848 revolution by Andrei Mureșanu, sung to a melody by Anton Pann.
